items.title: 16.2 Common types of hazards in a laboratory

blocks.text: Most hazards faced while working in the laboratory fall into three categories: physical, chemical and biological hazards. Each is described in the next three topics.

blocks.caption: The three categories
rows: slips and falls on a wet floor; cuts from broken glassware
the particular hazards of each chemical, handled by its standard procedure
allergens; infectious diseases passed from animals to humans; viral diseases

blocks.prompt: Classify these: a cracked beaker, a bottle of concentrated acid, a culture of mould (Quick Check 16.1a; exercise Q.3).
blocks.explanation: The cracked beaker is a physical hazard (cuts); the concentrated acid is a chemical hazard (burns, fumes); the mould culture is a biological hazard (allergens, infection).

items: Laboratory hazards: physical, chemical and biological.
